what_it_does: After a chip has been manufactured and a bug is discovered, engineers issue an ECO (Engineering Change Order) — a minimal patch that fixes the logic error with as few circuit changes as possible. The key step is finding the right "rectification signal" — a wire or internal node in the existing circuit that, if connected differently, would correct the faulty behavior. Choosing the best rectification signal among many candidates is currently done in an ad hoc, inefficient way. This paper presents a systematic method for collecting all valid candidate rectification signals, grouping and ranking them by how likely they are to produce a small, clean patch, and then efficiently checking which combinations actually fix the bug. The approach is validated with open-source patch generation tools and produces near-optimal patches faster than prior approaches.
